target_customer: Wine drinkers who want to taste wines by the glass, and gift buyers including corporate gifting
problem: Buying full bottles to discover wines is costly and wasteful. Vinebox ships single-serving glass tubes of wine with tasting notes.
business_model: Consumer subscription box plus gifting and bottle sales

founders.name: Rachel Vodofsky
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the 2018 funding press release and on Wikipedia, which says the founders were lawyers. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Club W (later Winc)
competitors.what: Online wine club shipping three bottles a month from 39 USD

technical_complexity.rationale: A subscription e-commerce flow with fulfilment. The hard parts were packaging wine in sealed glass tubes and shipping alcohol across state laws, not software.

defensibility.rationale: The tube format was borrowed from French sampling tubes and could be copied. The company later said patented 100 ml tubes, which gave some protection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Wine clubs coexisted. Sugarwish bought Vinebox in October 2021.

market_need_then: A September 2015 TechCrunch piece noted many subscription services sell boxes of bottles, and positioned by-the-glass tasting as a different way to discover wine. The 12 Nights of Wine advent calendar launched in November 2016 and sold out in four weeks per Wikipedia.

branding.domain_note: Started at getvinebox.com and now uses vinebox.com (redirect confirmed). Acquisition date of the exact domain not found.

identity.logo: wordmark on a company logo page
identity.visual_style: hand-drawn glass tubes with each vineyard's label graphics, per TechCrunch 2015
identity.voice_and_tone: simplifies wine, tasting notes and ratings

branding.brand_signature: Single-serve wine tubes and the 12 Nights of Wine advent calendar
branding.community_and_virality: Trend Hunter covered the vials and seasonal boxes; the advent calendar sold out in four weeks in 2016 per Wikipedia.

brand_strength.rationale: A memorable format and a seasonal hit product with press coverage, and the brand survived under a new owner.

outcome_analysis: Vinebox sold wine by the glass in tubes, joined YC W16, raised 1.25 million USD in 2016 and 5.9 million in 2018, and had a hit holiday product in the advent calendar. It was acquired by Sugarwish in October 2021 for an undisclosed price, and the brand still sells in 2026. The YC page lists it as inactive, which conflicts with the live brand. The format and seasonal brand drew attention, though no source links the brand to the exit price.
notes: The 1.25M USD round of March 2016 rests on Wikipedia alone (single outlet); investors are assumed from the YC batch only and not stated there. The 5.9M round is dated January 2018 by the press release and January 2019 by Seedtable and Bouncewatch, with the lead named as Harbinger Ventures by the press release and FinSMEs and as TMT Investments by Seedtable; Subscription Insider corrected a Series A label to seed. CB Insights total of about 6.57M across six rounds does not match the sum of the recorded rounds, so rounds may be missing. YC lists status Inactive although the acquirer operates the brand; the YC founder profile calls Vinebox acquired. Confidence is marked high because founders, competitor and funding are all sourced, but the competitor list is thin.
